questions.q: Rubidium is below potassium. Predict and explain its reaction with water, including a balanced equation. Portal response box.
questions.a: Reacts more vigorously than potassium/explosively (1); because reactivity increases down Group 1 (1); forms rubidium hydroxide and hydrogen (1); 2Rb + 2H₂O → 2RbOH + H₂ (2)
questions.model: Teacher writes the first point: 'Rubidium would react more violently than potassium, because reactivity increases down Group 1.'

questions.q: Why are Group 1 metals stored under oil?
questions.a: They react with oxygen and water vapour in air (1); oil keeps air and water away (1)

questions.q: Melting points: Li 181 °C, Na 98 °C, K 63 °C. Estimate Rb's and justify.
questions.a: About 40 °C (actual 39 °C): the trend decreases by smaller steps.

questions.q: Write the balanced equation for lithium with water.
questions.model: Same pattern as sodium: metal + water → hydroxide + hydrogen. Li + H₂O → LiOH + H₂. Hydrogens: 2 on the left need H₂ on the right, so double: 2Li + 2H₂O → 2LiOH + H₂.

questions.q: Describe two observations when sodium is added to water.
questions.a: Any two: floats; melts into a ball; moves around; fizzes; gets smaller and disappears

questions.q: Predict how caesium reacts with water.
questions.a: Explosively, forming caesium hydroxide and hydrogen
